claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has a dual-phase lamellar FCC/B2 microstructure.
The starting microstructure is hierarchical and organized into lamellar colonies.
Dislocations pile up at coarse or strongly ordered B2 lamellae or other internal boundaries.
Dislocation pile-ups create local stress concentrations that initiate microcracks and catastrophic tensile failure.
The untreated alloy has limited room-temperature tensile ductility and is brittle.
The proposed intervention is partial solution annealing at about 1150 °C for about 30 minutes followed by aging at about 700–800 °C for 2–4 hours.
The proposed heat treatment will refine and partially homogenize the B2 lamellae.
The proposed heat treatment will produce more coherent or semi-coherent interlamellar boundaries.
The proposed heat treatment will reduce the hardness or mechanical-property mismatch between the phases.
Improved boundary coherence and reduced phase mismatch will enhance dislocation transmission across internal interfaces.
Enhanced dislocation transmission will reduce pile-ups, local stress concentrations, microcrack initiation, and catastrophic failure.
The alloy contains a fine or nanoscale distribution of NiAl-rich precipitates that could be re-established by aging.
Aging after solution annealing will restore strengthening precipitates and thereby maintain or enhance strength.
The untreated alloy has an ultimate tensile strength of approximately 944 MPa.
The untreated alloy has approximately 25% tensile elongation.
The treated alloy will have an ultimate tensile strength of approximately 1000–1050 MPa at room temperature.
The treated alloy will have approximately 28–32% tensile elongation at room temperature.
The treatment will increase both tensile strength and ductility relative to the untreated alloy.
The predicted response applies to ambient room-temperature tensile testing at a strain rate of approximately 10^-3 s^-1.
Over-homogenization, phase coarsening, or inadequate precipitation during aging could prevent the predicted improvements.
